cards.text: Swarm after swarm of locusts has eaten up the land (Joel 1:4), and the priests are told to weep and pray that the LORD won't make His heritage a reproach, an object of scorn among the nations (Joel 2:17). And then, friend, the answer comes. The LORD becomes jealous for His land.

cards.question: The LORD is jealous for His land. What does He do for His people?

cards.text: Then the LORD answers His people, and friend, there's no hold music and no 'please stay on the line.' He ANSWERS.

cards.question: God tells His people what He'll send them, so they'll be satisfied. What is it?

answers.text: Grain and new wine and oil

cards.question: God tells His people He will never again make them a reproach among the nations.

cards.text: Next, God talks about the northern army. He'll drive it away to a barren and desolate land, and friend, that army is getting shown the DOOR.

cards.question: God splits up the northern army. Its front ranks go into the Eastern Sea, and its rear guard into the ___ Sea.

cards.text: And God says its stench will rise. Its foul odor will go up.
Then the words turn to the land itself: 'Do not be afraid, O land…' Friend, I spent years in the back of a junk drawer, and I would've given my whole mustache to hear that.

cards.question: The land is told not to be afraid, but to rejoice and be glad. Why?

answers.text: Because the LORD has done great things
Because the people have done great things
Because the enemy has begged for peace

cards.text: Now the beasts of the field hear it too: 'Do not be afraid…' I bet a few of those cows really needed that.

cards.question: The beasts of the field don't need to fear, because the open pastures have turned ___.
In the land, the fig tree and the vine hold back their best.

cards.text: First the land, then the animals, and now God's people, the children of Zion, are told to be glad and rejoice in the LORD their God. Friend, the good news is working its way down the WHOLE list.

cards.question: Zion's children have a reason to be glad. What has the LORD given them, as before?

answers.text: A new king on the throne

cards.text: And the text says those autumn rains are given for their vindication.

cards.question: The threshing floors will be ___ of grain, and the vats will ___ with new wine and oil.

cards.text: Then God speaks again, and He looks back at the years eaten by locusts. Friend, I lost YEARS in the back of a junk drawer, so I am LEANING IN for this one.

cards.question: What does God say He will do about the years eaten by locusts?

cards.text: REPAY the years, friend! Then God names who ate them: the swarming locust, the young locust, the destroying locust and the devouring locust.

cards.question: God has just named the four kinds of locusts. What does He call them?

answers.text: My great army that I sent

cards.text: God says they'll have plenty to eat until they're satisfied. Not last-crumbs-on-the-baking-sheet plenty, friend, PLENTY plenty.

cards.question: With plenty to eat, God's people will ___ the name of the LORD their God, who has worked wonders for them.

cards.text: The people who were called to weep (Joel 2:12) will be PRAISING, friend, and THAT is a comeback. And God says His people will never again be put to shame.
And here's the big finish. God says all of this leads to something His people will know.

cards.question: When God does all this, what will His people know?

answers.text: That God is present in Israel
That the harvest will last forever
That the locusts will never return

cards.question: God tells His people He is the LORD their God, and there is no other.
